questions.question: What is a rigid motion?
choices: A transformation that multiplies every length by 2
A transformation that preserves distances between points
A transformation that stretches only one dimension
A transformation that changes each angle by 10°

questions.question: Which transformation is a rigid motion?
How can congruent figures be related through transformations?
choices: Any enlargement maps one onto the other
Only a change in area can match them
A sequence of rigid motions maps one exactly onto the other

questions.question: What does a rigid motion preserve besides length?
Which dilation preserves all distances?
What is orientation in the context of a labeled polygon?
choices: The clockwise or counterclockwise order of its vertices

questions.question: Which single rigid motion reverses orientation?
Why can two congruent figures have different coordinates?
choices: Rigid motions may change position while preserving size and shape

questions.question: If a 7-unit segment is rotated by 135°, what is its image length?
What happens to a triangle's area under a translation?
choices: It changes by the translation distance

questions.question: Two reflections across the same line are performed in succession. What is the resulting transformation?
choices: A reflection across a perpendicular line

questions.question: Why is matching only area insufficient to prove congruence?
choices: Congruent figures always have unequal areas
Different shapes can have equal areas
Equal areas force equal side lengths

questions.question: Which comparison best supports congruence after a transformation?
choices: Only the figures' centers are equally high
Corresponding lengths and angles are unchanged
The figures have the same number of vertices
Both figures lie in the same quadrant

questions.question: A figure is reflected and then translated. Is the final image congruent to the original?
choices: Yes, both steps preserve distances and angles
No, any two-step transformation changes size
Only if the translation distance is zero
Only if the figure is a circle

questions.question: What happens to perimeter under any sequence of rigid motions?
choices: It changes by the number of steps
It depends on the rotation angle

questions.question: Two triangles have equal corresponding sides but opposite vertex orientation. Which type of motion may be needed to match their labeled vertices?
choices: A reflection as part of the matching sequence
A change to one side length

questions.question: A rectangle of dimensions 3 by 8 is compared with one of dimensions 4 by 6. Both have area 24. Are they congruent?
choices: No, their corresponding side lengths differ
No, congruent figures must have different areas

questions.question: A transformation maps every point by (x, y) → (x + 5, y + 2). Why is it rigid?
choices: The same vector shift leaves pairwise distances unchanged
Its coordinates always increase in absolute value

questions.question: A polygon is reflected twice across intersecting lines. Which conclusion about size is guaranteed?
choices: Its perimeter depends on the angle between the lines

questions.question: A student scales a triangle by 1/2, then translates it. Why is the final triangle generally not congruent to the original?
